questions.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay titled “Doviolent video games lead to violence?”. The statement given below is for your reference. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words . A growing body of research finds that violent video games can make kids act aggressively in their real world relationships, causing an increase in violence.
questions.correctAnswer:
Do Violent Video Games Lead to Violence?

The relationship between violent video games and real-life behavior deserves careful discussion. Research raising concerns about aggression should be taken seriously, but it does not mean that every player will become violent.

Repeated exposure to aggressive scenes may influence how some children respond to conflict, especially when they lack guidance. At the same time, family relationships, personal experiences and the social environment also shape behavior. It would be too simple to blame one type of entertainment for every incident. Parents and teachers should therefore pay attention to a child's overall habits instead of judging by a game alone.

In my opinion, age-appropriate choices and reasonable time limits are important. Adults can discuss the difference between fictional action and acceptable behavior, encourage cooperative activities and notice worrying changes early. A balanced approach protects children while avoiding unsupported claims. The goal should be responsible entertainment and healthy relationships, not a careless argument about games.

questions.explanation:
以下为按题意独立写成的参考范文，作文没有唯一答案。区分aggression与实际violence，承认研究关注但不推断每个玩家都会暴力；结论提出年龄适配、讨论与时间管理。

题面标题Doviolent缺少空格，按Do violent video games lead to violence?理解并规范范文标题，未改动原题。文章先承认关注，再区分可能影响和必然暴力，最后写年龄适配与引导。act aggressively表示表现得有攻击性，lead to表示导致，不能将might写成must。讨论不需编造研究人数；用具体使用条件说明观点，比只答yes或no充分。自查标题、主体和结论都围绕暴力游戏，而非所有游戏。

练习方法：先用提示列三段提纲，在30分钟内独立写作，再按下方标准逐项打分；把失分最多的一段重写。参考范文约159词（缩写、连字符词按一词，含标题或书信称呼落款），满足120–180词要求；评分用于练习自检，不代表官方阅卷分数。
rubric: 练习自评总分15分：题目覆盖0–6＋结构0–4＋语言0–5，先独立写完再对照；观点不同于范文也可得满分，只要有合理支持。
题目覆盖0–6分：该题检查——回应暴力游戏与现实行为的关系，同时考虑其他影响因素。。6分=任务完整且有具体理由/活动/例证；4–5分=切题但细节偏薄；2–3分=遗漏主要任务；0–1分=基本离题。
结构0–4分：4分=开头明确任务、主体按逻辑展开、结尾回扣，段间自然；3分=顺序清楚但局部衔接生硬；1–2分=跳跃或机械罗列；0分=内容难以组织理解。
语言0–5分：5分=语法和用词基本准确、句型有变化；3–4分=少量错误但不影响理解；1–2分=反复出现时态、主谓一致或搭配错误并影响阅读；0分=多数句子不能理解。
格式与修订：按原题保持120–180词；新闻/书信/提案用对应体裁，明确要求的首句逐字保留。若超限、少写任务或缺必要格式，先修改再评分，不把字数达标当作内容满分。

questions.prompt: Being a close loser could greatly motivate one to persevere in their research.
questions.passage:
Science of setbacks: How failure can improve career prospects

A) How do early career setbacks affect our long-term success? Failures can help us learn and overcome our fears. But disasters can still wound us. They can screw us up and set us back. Wouldn't it be nice if there was genuine, scientifically documented truth to the expression "what doesn't kill you makes you stronger"?

B) One way social scientists have probed the effects of career setbacks is to look at scientists of very similar qualifications. These scientists, for reasons that are mostly arbitrary, either just missed getting a research grant or just barely made it. In social sciences, this is known as examining "near misses" and "narrow wins" in areas where merit is subjective. That allows researchers to measure only the effects of being chosen or not. Studies in this area have found conflicting results. In the competitive game of biomedical science, research has been done on scientists who narrowly lost or won grant money. Why is this happening? We can point to at least three potential causes. One is the rise in obesity levels itself. Under-reporting rates are much higher for obese people, because they simply consume more food, and thus have more to remember.

Another cause is that the proportion of people who are trying to lose weight has been increasing over time. People who want to lose weight are more likely to under-report their eating—regardless of whether they are overweight or not. This may be driven partly by self-deception or "wishful thinking".

The final potential cause is an increase in snacking and eating out over recent decades—both in terms of how often they happen and how much they contribute to our overall energy intake. Again, there is evidence that food consumed out of the home is one of the most poorly recorded categories in surveys.

If people do not know how much they are eating, it can be really hard for them to stick to a diet. Also, we should be looking for new ways to ensure what people eat wouldn't have much impact on their waistlines. If this works, it won't matter if they can't remember what they ate yesterday.
